minutes.summary: The Parks Commission discussed opening the 2022 beach season with the beach house front wall under repair, including portable toilets and asbestos testing. It recommended hiring a beach director and four lifeguards, kept beach rates unchanged, and weighed in on Marshall Park design alternatives, favoring Alternative One with modifications.

Beach house repairs, asbestos, portable toilets and DPW support
Recreation director update on portable toilets

topics.resolution: preference for Alternative One with modifications

votes.motion: Approve January 6 minutes as revised, January 20 and March 8 as presented
Recommend to the town manager appointment of the beach director and four named lifeguards
Keep beach passes and rates at the same cost as last year

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to keep 2022 beach passes and daily rates at last year's level.
It voted to recommend to the town manager a beach director and four named lifeguards.
The commission favored Marshall Park Alternative One with an extra trail, separately priced pond park and court area, and a moved entry sidewalk.
The recreation director will work on portable toilet placement and a safe barrier by the old playground, and report back next month.
The beach house front wall repair estimate exceeded the procurement threshold and missed the FY23 capital planning process.

why_it_matters: Beach pass prices stay as they were for the 2022 season, though swim lesson fees, which are meant to cover lifeguard cost, are still undecided.
The beach house wall repair is not in the FY23 capital plan, so it will draw on the facilities budget and contracted services, and Marshall Park has no identified funding source yet.
watch_next: Next meeting April 13 at 7 p.m. by Zoom, with the consultant presenting the final Marshall Park design.
Swim lesson fees are due to be taken up at the next meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both votes (beach appointments and keeping pass rates) and on the Marshall Park preference for Alternative One. The one thing to know is that the official minutes leave out much of what the recording covers: the portable toilet discussion, the beach house repair amount, swim lesson fees and the next-meeting date. The only figure that differs is a likely caption error, $23 in ours against $25 in the official reading of the rates.
